summary:
Disegni and Liu prove the p-adic analogue of the arithmetic inner product formula of Li–Liu — equivalently, the first p-adic Gross–Zagier formula in genuinely higher dimension. Let E/F be a CM extension in which every p-adic place splits, and π a relevant representation of the quasi-split unitary group G_r = U(W_r) of rank n = 2r, Panchishkin unramified (ordinary for the Siegel parabolic) above p.

- **The p-adic L-function (§§2–3, Theorem 1.4).** A cyclotomic p-adic L-function L^♦_p(π) on the character space of Γ_{F,p} is constructed by the doubling method, from a family of explicit big-cell sections f^{[e]}_{χ_p} on which the U_p-operators act by translation. The rationality is proved on Siegel hermitian varieties over Q_p compared with PEL moduli, so the interpolation holds along every isomorphism Q_p ≃ C.
- **Selmer theta lifts (§4).** The θ_π-part V_{π,L} of H^{2r−1}_ét(X_L) and the canonical map ℘_π give Kudla's generating series a Selmer-group avatar; under the Modularity Hypothesis its convolution with a form in π̂ is a Selmer theta lift in H^1_f(E, V_{π,L}).
- **The formula (Theorems 1.7, 1.8).** If ord_{χ=1}L^♦_p(π) = 1 then the generating function is modular, and the Nekovář p-adic height of two Selmer theta lifts equals ∂L^♦_p(π) times explicit gamma factors and local doubling zeta integrals. Corollaries 1.9 and 1.12 give H^1_f(E, ρ_π(r)) ≠ 0, in particular for symmetric powers of ordinary modular elliptic curves.
- **Method.** The local heights away from p are the Beilinson local indices of Li–Liu (through Scholl's comparison); above p they are shown to tend to 0 p-adically along the U_p-iteration, which needs a new crystalline property of bi-extensions (Theorem A.8) proved in Appendix B through log syntomic cohomology, rigid de Rham–Witt complexes, log rigid cohomology with proper support and de Jong's alterations.

The libraries have none of this. The atlas plans the surrounding theory — Selmer structures (SelmerIwasawaCohomology), period rings and comparisons (PadicHodgeTheory, CohomologyComparisons, CrystallineCohomology, rigid cohomology), the doubling p-adic L-function for ordinary unitary groups (AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4), the Weil representation (MP.2–MP.3), cycle classes (EDC.3) and continuous cohomology (D7) — but not p-adic heights.

Routes: two new Part IIs, PadicArithmeticInnerProductFormula (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights) for the Selmer theta lifts and the formula itself, and SelmerComplexesAndPadicHeights (parent SelmerIwasawaCohomology) for Nekovář's height pairing, bi-extensions and Theorem A.8; and sources for AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4–L5, MetaplecticAutomorphicForms MP.2–MP.3, PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology RD.4, CrystallineCohomology CR.4–CR.6 and PadicHodgeTheory R06.1.

Seven groups of misprints are recorded; no mathematical error or gap was found. The paper's own §4.10 records two errata for Li–Liu I and II, which are noted here and in those extractions.

items.name: Theorem 1.4 = Theorem 3.37 (the cyclotomic p-adic L-function of π)
items.statement: Let E/F be a CM extension of number fields in which every p-adic place of F splits, n = 2r, G_r = U(W_r) quasi-split, and π a relevant L-representation of G_r(A^∞_F) (Definition 1.1) with π_v Panchishkin unramified for every v | p. For every finite set ♦ of places of Q containing {∞, p} outside which π is unramified there is a unique bounded analytic function L^♦_p(π) on X_{F,p} ⊗_{Q_p} L (equivalently, an L-valued p-adic measure on Γ_{F,p}) such that for every finite character χ : Γ_{F,p} → Q_p^× and every embedding ι : Q_p → C, ιL^♦_p(π)(χ) = (1/P^ι_π)·(Z_r^{[F:Q]}/b^♦_{2r}(1))·Π_{v|p}Π_{u ∈ P_v} γ((1+r)/2, ι(π_u ⊗ χ_v), ψ_{F,v})^{−1}·L(1/2, BC(ιπ^♦) ⊗ (ιχ^♦ ∘ Nm_{E/F})), where P^ι_π is the period of Notation 3.15, Z_r = (−1)^r 2^{−r²−r}π^{r²}Γ(1)⋯Γ(r)/(Γ(r+1)⋯Γ(2r)) is the archimedean doubling zeta integral, and b^♦_{2r}(1) = Π_{i=1}^{2r} L^♦(i, η^i_{E/F}).
items.locator: Theorem 1.4 and Remark 1.5, pp. 223–224; Theorem 3.37 and proof, pp. 268–271, published version
items.note: Remark 1.5: the periods are well defined up to L^×, the vanishing order at 1 is independent of ♦, L^♦_p(π) = L^♦_p(π̂), and the interpolation is along all isomorphisms Q_p ≃ C (a stronger rationality than in [17] = Eischen–Harris–Li–Skinner, whose ordinary construction it overlaps). items.name: Theorem 1.8 = Theorem 4.21 (the p-adic arithmetic inner product formula)

items.name: Corollary 1.9 and Corollary 1.12 (evidence for the p-adic Beilinson–Bloch–Kato conjecture; symmetric powers)
items.statement: Corollary 1.9: in the situation of Assumption 1.6 with n < p, if ord_{χ=1}L^♦_p(π) = 1 then dim_{Q_p} H^1_f(E, ρ_π(r)) ≥ 1. Corollary 1.12: for a modular elliptic curve A over F without CM, ordinary at every p-adic place, with π = π(Sym^{n−1}A_E) the transfer of Π(Sym^{n−1}A) (automorphy of symmetric powers of Hilbert modular forms, [59]), and under n < p, [F : Q] > 1, r[F : Q] odd, every prime of V^{ram}_F unramified over Q, and V^A_F ∪ V^{(2)}_F ⊆ V^{spl}_F: L^♦_p(π)(1) = 0, and if ∂L^♦_p(π)(1) ≠ 0 then dim_{Q_p} H^1_f(E, Sym^{n−1}H^1_ét(A_E, Q_p)(r)) ≥ 1.

items.name: Definition 1.1, Assumption 1.6 and Assumption 4.23 (relevant representations and the running hypotheses)
items.statement: Definition 1.1: a relevant L-representation of G_r(A^∞_F) is π with coefficients in L such that for every ι : L → C, (⊗_{v|∞}π^{[r]}_v) ⊗ ιπ is a tempered cuspidal automorphic representation of G_r(A_F), π^{[r]}_v being the holomorphic discrete series with Harish–Chandra parameter ((n−1)/2, …, 1/2; −1/2, …, −(n−1)/2). Assumption 1.6: F ≠ Q; V^{spl}_F contains all 2-adic and p-adic places; every prime of V^{ram}_F is unramified over Q; π_v is spherical for v ∈ V^{ram}_F, unramified or almost unramified for v ∈ V^{int}_F (almost unramified only at v unramified over Q), R_π ∪ S_π ⊆ V^♥_F, and π_v is Panchishkin unramified for every v | p. Assumption 4.23: the set of primes of E above R is nonempty and generates the relative class group of E/F.

items.name: Definitions 3.18, 3.21 and Lemmas 3.19–3.25 (Panchishkin unramified representations)
items.statement: For u ∈ P_v the Satake polynomial P_{π_u}(T) = Π_j(T − α_{u,j}√q_v^{n−1}) has the form T^n + Σ_s β_{u,s}q^{s(s−1)/2}_vT^{n−s} with β_{u,s} ∈ O_L (Lemma 3.19), the multiset A(π_u, m) := {(Π_{j ∈ J}α_{u,j})√q_v^{m(n−m)} : J ⊆ {1, …, n}, |J| = m} lies in Z_p and meets Z^×_p in at most one element, which happens iff β_{u,m} ∈ O^×_L. π_v is Panchishkin unramified if β_{u,r} ∈ O^×_L for u ∈ P_v (Definition 3.21); this holds for π_v iff it holds for π̂_v (Lemma 3.22), and is equivalent to ordinarity at v for the Siegel parabolic in Hida's sense (Remark 1.3). Lemma 3.20 identifies the generalized eigenvalues of the operators T^±_u on π^{I_v}_v with A(π_u, r) and A(π_{u^c}, r); Lemma 3.23 and Notation 3.24 produce the canonical lines π^±_v and the units α(π_u); Proposition 3.25 produces the unique divisor Q_{π_u}(T) = T^r + γ_{u,1}T^{r−1} + γ_{u,2}q_vT^{r−2} + ⋯ + γ_{u,r}q^{r(r−1)/2}_v of P_{π_u}(T) with γ_{u,r} ∈ O^×_L, hence the unramified principal series π_u of GL_r(F_v), together with the locally constant function ξ_{π_v} on G_r(F_v) used in the p-adic zeta integral.
items.locator: §3.3, Definitions 3.18, 3.21, Lemmas 3.19–3.20, 3.22–3.23, Notation 3.24, Proposition 3.25, pp. 257–261, published version
items.note: Routed to AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4–L5 as a source.

items.name: §3.4 (local doubling zeta integrals: Lemma 3.26, Definition 3.27, Lemmas 3.29–3.31 and Proposition 3.32)
items.statement: Lemma 3.26 (from [46]): with ς(a, u_1, u_2) := (1_r, u_2; 0, 1_r)(−a, 0; 0, −{}^ta^{c,−1})w_r(1_r, u_1; 0, 1_r) mapping into the big Bruhat cell, the doubling zeta integral Z^ι(ϕ^∨_v ⊗ ϕ_v, f) is an integral over (Res_{E/F}GL_r) × Herm × Herm of the Fourier transform of f against matrix coefficients. Definition 3.27 defines (ϕ^∨_v, ϕ_v)-typical elements f ∈ S(Herm_{2r}(F_v)) by conditions on f̂ (rationality, support in the standard set and a normalized integral), which exist whenever ⟨π^∨_v(w_r)ϕ^∨_v, ϕ_v⟩ ∈ Q^× (Remark 3.28); for such f and unramified χ_v, Z^ι(ϕ^∨_v ⊗ ϕ_v, f_{χ_v}) = 1 (Lemma 3.29). Lemma 3.30: for a Q-valued section f the zeta integral is a single element Z(ϕ^∨_v ⊗ ϕ_v, f) ∈ L interpolating all Z^ι. Lemma 3.31 (Piatetski-Shapiro–Rallis): for v ∤ p unramified, Z^ι(ϕ^∨_v ⊗ ϕ_v, f^{sph}_{χ_v}) = L(1/2, BC(ιπ_v) ⊗ (χ_v ∘ Nm))/b_{2r,v}(χ). Proposition 3.32: for v | p with π_v Panchishkin unramified, ∫_{G_r(F_v)}ιξ_{π_v}(g)(f^{[0]}_{χ_v})_{χ_v}(w_r(g, 1_{2r}))dg = q^{d_vr²}_vΠ_{u ∈ P_v}γ((1+r)/2, ιπ_u ⊗ χ_v, ψ_{F,v})^{−1}.
items.locator: §3.4, Lemma 3.26, Definition 3.27, Remark 3.28, Lemmas 3.29–3.31, Proposition 3.32, pp. 262–265, published version
items.note: Proposition 3.32 is where the gamma factors of Theorem 1.4 appear; the proof needs no explicit section at p, only the Fourier transform. Routed to AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4–L5 as a source.

items.name: §3.5 (Lemmas 3.33–3.34, Notation 3.35, Definition 3.36 and Lemma 3.38: the construction of L^♦_p(π))
items.statement: For ‖e‖ > 0 the pullbacks h̃_{r,r}(D̃^{[e]}_♦(−, Ω)) lie in the limit of H̃^{[r]}_{r,r}(K̃_{r,r}(p^dΔ, Δ′)) (Lemma 3.33) and descend to elements D^{[e]}_♦(−, Ω) over Q_p (Lemma 3.34); with pr_{π,π̂} = pr_π ⊗ pr_{π̂} and the pairing ⟨ϕ_1 ⊗ ϕ_2, Ψ⟩_{π,π̂} (Notation 3.35), Definition 3.36 sets L^♦_p(π)(Ω) := (Π_{u ∈ P}α(π_u))^{−1}⟨ϕ_1 ⊗ ϕ_2, D^{[1]}_♦(−, Ω)⟩_{π,π̂} for open compact Ω ⊆ Γ_{F,p}. Lemma 3.38: for each finite χ there is e_χ with (f^{[e]}_{χ_p})_{χ_p} invariant under the relevant Iwahori-type subgroups once e_u ≥ e_χ.
items.locator: §3.5, Lemmas 3.33–3.34, Notation 3.35, Definition 3.36, Lemma 3.38, pp. 265–268, 271, published version

items.name: Proposition 3.39 and Remark 3.40 (parity of the vanishing order)
items.statement: The vanishing order of L^♦_p(π) at 1 has the same parity as r[F : Q] + (1 − ϵ(π))/2, where ϵ(π) is the global root number; the proof factors the complex L-function into the local factors L_p(π_v) for v ∈ V^{(♦\{∞,p})}_F and compares with the functional equation. Remark 3.40 expects the resulting L_p(π) to again be a p-adic measure.
items.locator: Proposition 3.39 and Remark 3.40, pp. 271–272, published version
items.note: Routed to AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4–L5 as a source.

items.name: §3.6 (derivatives of p-adic measures: ∂_λμ, Definition 3.41 and Lemma 3.42)
items.statement: For an L-valued p-adic measure μ on Γ_{F,p}, μ(χ) = ∫χdμ = lim_d Σ_{x ∈ Γ_d}χ(x)vol(xU_d, μ); the derivative along λ ∈ Hom_{Z_p}(Γ_{F,p}, Z_p) is ∂_λμ = lim_d Σ_x λ(x)vol(xU_d, μ), and ∂μ ∈ Γ^{fr}_{F,p} ⊗ L collects them. μ is integral if vol(Ω, μ) ∈ O_L for every Ω (Definition 3.41), and then ∂_λμ − Σ_{x ∈ Γ_d}λ(x)vol(xU_d, μ) ∈ p^dO_L for every d (Lemma 3.42).
items.locator: §3.6, (3.18), Definition 3.41, Lemma 3.42, pp. 272–274, published version

items.name: §4.1(H1)–(H9) (hermitian spaces, Weil representations, Siegel–Weil sections and the Siegel–Weil measure)
items.statement: For a hermitian space V over E of rank n with signature (n−1, 1) at v_0 and (n, 0) elsewhere, H = U(V), with moment map T(x) = ((x_i, x_j))_{i,j}, the regular locus (V^m_v)^{reg}, good lattices (index q^{1−ϵ_v}_v in the dual) and good level subgroups and Schwartz functions; the Weil representation ω_{m,v} of G_m(F_v) × H(F_v) on S(V^m_v, M) with ω(m(a))φ(x) = |det a|^r_{E_v}φ(xa), ω(n(b))φ(x) = ψ_{F,v}(tr bT(x))φ(x), ω(w_m)φ = γ^m_{V_v,ψ}φ̂ and ω(h)φ(x) = φ(h^{−1}x); the Siegel–Weil section f^{SW}_Φ(g) = (ω_{2r,v}(g)Φ)(0) ∈ I□_{r,v}(1); and the Siegel–Weil measure dh_v, the unique Q-valued Haar measure with I_{T□}(Φ) = ∫_{H(F_v)}Φ(h^{−1}x)dh_v = b_{2r,v}(1)·W_{T□}(f^{SW}_Φ) for x in (V^{2r}_v)_{T□}, giving hyperspecial subgroups volume 1 at unramified places. (H6) fixes the spherical Hecke algebras T^♦ and their split-supported subrings S^♦.
items.locator: §4.1(H1)–(H9), pp. 274–276, published version
items.note: Routed to MetaplecticAutomorphicForms MP.2–MP.3 as a source, as PAPER-LI-LIU-22 routes the same material.

items.name: Lemma 4.1, Definition 4.2, Remark 4.3 and Lemma 4.5 (local theta dichotomy, π-coherence and rationality of theta lifts)
items.statement: Lemma 4.1: for every v there is a unique hermitian space V_{π_v} of rank n with θ(ιπ_v) ≠ 0 exactly when V_v ≅ V_{π_v}, in which case θ(ιπ_v) is tempered irreducible and Hom_{H(F_v)}(S(V^r_{π_v}), θ(ιπ_v)) ≅ ιπ_v (local theta dichotomy [20 = Gong–Grenié], [25 = Harris–Kudla–Sweet], [18 = Gan–Ichino], [24 = Harris]). Definition 4.2: V is π-coherent if V_v ≅ V_{π_v} for all finite v; Remark 4.3: such V exists iff Π_v η_{E/F}((−1)^r det V_{π_v}) = −(−1)^{r[F:Q]} (4.1), and then L^♦_p(π) vanishes at 1. Lemma 4.5: θ(σιπ_v) ≅ σθ(ιπ_v) for σ ∈ Aut(C/Q_π), where Q_π is the field of (4.2) generated by quadratic data at the ramified places (Remark 4.4: Q_π = Q under Assumption 1.6, and p is unramified in Q_π).
items.locator: §4.1, Lemma 4.1, Definition 4.2, Remarks 4.3–4.4, Lemma 4.5, pp. 276–278, published version
items.note: Routed to MetaplecticAutomorphicForms MP.3 as a source, as PAPER-LI-LIU-21 routes the local theta dichotomy there.

items.name: Lemmas 4.6–4.8 (the θ_π-isotypic part V_{π,L} and the canonical map ℘_π)
items.statement: Lemma 4.6: H^{2r−1}_ét(X_L, L_π(r)) decomposes canonically as the θ_π-part V_{π,L} plus the θ̂_π-part, compatibly with all ι (Matsushima). Lemma 4.7: there is a unique map ℘_π : H^{2r}_ét(X_L, L_π(r)) → H^1(E, V_{π,L}) vanishing on F²H^{2r} and inducing the inclusion on the H^1-graded piece of the Hochschild–Serre filtration; its existence uses an element s ∈ S^♦_L annihilating H^{2r} and acting as the identity on the θ_π-part ([46, Prop. 6.9(1)]). Lemma 4.8: for good L^♦ and s ∈ S^♦_{π,L}, s^* = χ^♦_{π̂}(s)·℘_π, and the restriction of χ^♦_{π̂} to S^♦_{π,L} is surjective under the stated hypotheses.
items.locator: Lemmas 4.6–4.8, pp. 278–280, published version
items.note: Routed to the new Part II PadicArithmeticInnerProductFormula (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Lemmas 4.9–4.10, Hypothesis 4.11 and Lemmas 4.13–4.14 (the Galois representation ρ_π and the local conditions)
items.statement: Lemma 4.9: V_{π,L} is crystalline at every place above an unramified v | p (via a finite étale cover with smooth reduction, [63 = Rapoport–Smithling–Zhang, Thm. 4.5]). Lemma 4.10: there is a unique semisimple ρ_π of Gal(E̅/E) of dimension n with the Satake characteristic polynomials at split places outside ♦, and ρ_{π̂} ≅ ρ^c_π ≅ ρ^∨_π(1−n) (using the endoscopic classification [54 = Mok] and [10 = Chenevier–Harris]). Hypothesis 4.11: every irreducible subquotient of V_{π,L} ⊗_{L_π,ι}Q_p is a direct summand of ρ_π(r) (expected from a sequel to [36 = Kisin–Shin–Zhu]). Lemma 4.13: H^i(E_u, V_{π,L}) = 0 for u ∤ p, by purity of WD(ρ_π(r)|_{E_u}) ([8, 9 = Caraiani], [70 = Taylor–Yoshida], [58 = Nekovář]). Lemma 4.14: for v | p with π_v Panchishkin unramified, V_{π,L}|_{E_u} and V_{π̂,L}|_{E_u} satisfy the Panchishkin condition of Definition A.12 and are pure of weight −1.
items.locator: Lemmas 4.9–4.10, Hypothesis 4.11, Remark 4.12, Lemmas 4.13–4.14, pp. 280–282, published version
items.note: Routed to the new Part II PadicArithmeticInnerProductFormula (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: The p-adic height pairing (4.4) on the θ_π-parts
items.statement: If π_v is Panchishkin unramified for every v | p, then the hypotheses (V1)–(V3) of §A.7 hold for K = E, X = X_L, d = d′ = r, V = V_{π,L} and V′ = V_{π̂,L}, so Nekovář's theory gives a canonical p-adic height pairing ⟨ , ⟩_{(V_{π,L},V_{π̂,L}),E} : H^1_f(E, V_{π,L}) × H^1_f(E, V_{π̂,L}) → Γ_{E,p} ⊗_{Z_p}L_π, defined through the canonical Hodge splittings at the p-adic places.
items.locator: §4.2, (4.4), p. 282, published version
items.note: Routed to the new Part II PadicArithmeticInnerProductFormula (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: §4.3 (Kudla's special cycles, Z_T(φ)_L and the étale classes)
items.statement: For x ∈ V^m ⊗_F A^∞_F, Kudla's special cycle Z(x)_L ∈ Z^m(X_L) (when T(x) ∈ Herm°_m(F)^+, and in CH^m(X_L)_Q in general); for a Schwartz function φ, Z_T(φ)_L = Σ_{x ∈ L\V^m⊗A^∞, T(x)=T}φ(x)Z(x)_L, with image Z^ét_T(φ)_L ∈ H^{2m}_ét(X_L, Q_p(m)) ⊗ M under the absolute cycle class map.

items.name: Definition 4.15, Hypothesis 4.16, Remark 4.17 and Proposition 4.18 (Selmer generating functions and their rationality)
items.statement: Definition 4.15: the π-Selmer generating function is Z^π_φ(g)_L := Σ_{T ∈ Herm_r(F)^+}℘_π(Z^ét_T(ω_r(g)φ)_L)q^T ∈ H^1(E, V_{π,L}) ⊗ SF_r(L ⊗_Q C). Hypothesis 4.16 (Modularity): for every φ there exists Z^π_{φ,L} ∈ H^1_f(E, V_{π,L}) ⊗_{Q_π}A^{[r]}_{r,hol} with (1 ⊗ q^{an}_r)(g·Z^π_{φ,L}) = Z^π_φ(g)_L for every g; it is implied by [46, Hypothesis 4.5] and is stronger than its ι-by-ι version (Remark 4.17). Proposition 4.18: under Hypothesis 4.16 the form is defined over the coefficient field, i.e. there is a unique Z^π_{φ,L} ∈ H^1_f(E, V_{π,L}) ⊗_{L_π}(V_π ⊗_Q M) inducing all (Z^π_{φ,L})^ι.
items.locator: Definition 4.15, Hypothesis 4.16, Remark 4.17, Proposition 4.18, pp. 282–284, published version

items.name: Definition 4.19 and §4.4 (Selmer theta lifts and the canonical height)
items.statement: Θ^{Sel}_φ(ϕ)_L := ⟨ϕ^†, Z^π_{φ,L}⟩_π ∈ H^1_f(E, V_{π,L}) ⊗_{Q_π}M is the Selmer theta lift, compatible under pullback in L; it is the Selmer-group analogue of the arithmetic theta lift of [46, 49]. With the canonical volume vol^♮(L) of [46, Definition 3.8] (the product of W_{2r} and the Siegel–Weil volume of L), the height vol^♮(L)⟨Θ^{Sel}_{φ_1}(ϕ_1)_L, Θ^{Sel}_{φ_2}(ϕ_2)_L⟩_{(V_{π,L},V_{π̂,L}),E} is independent of L and is written ⟨Θ^{Sel}_{φ_1}(ϕ_1), Θ^{Sel}_{φ_2}(ϕ_2)⟩^♮_{π,E}.

items.name: §4.5 (Lemmas 4.24, 4.26, 4.27 and Definition 4.25: reducing modularity to a height identity)
items.statement: Lemma 4.24: if π_v is unramified for every v | p, the image of CH^r(X_L) → H^{2r}_ét(X_L, Q_p(r)) → H^1(E, V_{π,L}) lies in H^1_f ([58, Thm. 3.1]). Definition 4.25: ϕ ∈ L ⊗_Q A^{[r]}_{r,hol} is strongly nonzero if ιϕ ≠ 0 for every ι. Lemma 4.26: if for some L, φ_1, ζ ∈ H^1_f(E, V_{π̂,L}), λ ∈ Hom_{Z_p}(Γ_{E,p}, Z_p) and a strongly nonzero ϕ_1 one has (1 × q^{an}_r)(g·ϕ_1) = Σ_T λ⟨℘_π(Z^ét_T(ω_r(g)φ_1)_L), ζ⟩_E q^T for all g ∈ G_r(A^∞_F), then Hypothesis 4.16 holds for every φ. Lemma 4.27: an identity of this shape for all g ∈ M_r(F_R) already propagates to all g ∈ G_r(A^∞_F), by a strengthening of Kudla's formal modularity ([49, Theorem 3.5]) using Assumption 4.23.

items.name: Notation 4.28 and §4.5(S1)–(S4) (the pool of Schwartz functions and Lemma 4.29)
items.statement: For v ∈ R a regular pair (φ_{v,1}, φ_{v,2}) with support in (V^{2r}_v)^{reg}; for v ∈ T the characteristic functions of a good lattice; for v | p a polarization Λ_v = Λ_{v,1} ⊕ p^{−d_v}_vΛ_{v,2} into isotropic O_{E_v}-submodules and, for e ∈ N^{P_v}, the subsets Λ^{[e]}_{v,1}, Λ^{[e]}_{v,2} of (ϖ^{−e−ε_v}_vΛ_{v,1} ⊕ ϖ^{−e+ε^c_v}_vΛ_{v,2})^r, resp. (ϖ^{−e}_vΛ_v)^r, with integral moment matrix and prescribed generation, giving φ^{[e]}_{v,i}. Lemma 4.29: U^{e′}_vφ^{[e]}_{v,i} = φ^{[e+e′]}_{v,i}; φ^{[e]}_{v,i} is L_v-fixed; the support of φ^{[e_1]}_{v,1} ⊗ φ^{[e_2]}_{v,2} is regular and f^{SW}_{φ^{[e_1]}_{v,1} ⊗ φ^{[e_2]}_{v,2}} = b_{2r,v}(1)^{−1}vol(L_v, dh_v)(f^{[e^c_1+ε^c_v+e_2]}_{1_v})_{1_v} (4.7), matching the sections of Construction 3.8.
items.locator: Notation 4.28, §4.5(S1)–(S4), Lemma 4.29, pp. 291–293, published version

items.name: The decomposition (4.8) of the global height into local heights
items.statement: For cycles with disjoint support (guaranteed by the regularity in §4.5(S1)), the p-adic height pairing of their classes decomposes as ⟨Z^ét_{T_1}(s_1φ^{[e_1]}_1)_L, Z^ét_{T_2}(s_2φ^{[e_2]}_2)_L⟩_E = Σ_{u ∤ ∞}⟨Z_{T_1}(s_1φ^{[e_1]}_1)_L, Z_{T_2}(s_2φ^{[e_2]}_2)_L⟩_{E_u} in Γ_{E,p} ⊗_{Z_p}L, by the theory of §A.7.
items.locator: §4.5, (4.8), p. 293, published version

items.name: §4.6 (Lemma 4.31, Notation 4.32 and Proposition 4.33: local heights away from p)
items.statement: Lemma 4.31: for v ∈ T the Whittaker values of the standard Siegel–Weil section are a polynomial W_{T□,v} ∈ Z[X] in χ_v(ϖ_v) after multiplying by b_{2r,v}(χ) ([47, Rem. 2.18, Lemma 2.19], [48, §9]). Notation 4.32: Diff(T□, V) = {v : (V^{2r}_v)_{T□} = ∅} is finite of odd cardinality, and Herm°_{2r}(F)^+_V is where it is a singleton v_{T□}. Proposition 4.33: there exists (t_1, t_2) with χ^♦_{π̂}(t_1)χ^♦_π(t_2) ≠ 0 such that Nm_{E/F}(vol^♮(L)Σ_{u ∤ ∞p}⟨Z_{T_1}(t_1s_1φ^{[e_1]}_1)_L, Z_{T_2}(t_2s_2φ^{[e_2]}_2)_L⟩_{E_u}) equals W_{2r}Σ_{T□ ∈ Herm°_{2r}(F)^+_V, ∂_{r,r}T□=(T_1,T_2)}W′_{T□,v_{T□}}(1)I_{T□}(⋯)[v_{T□}] plus the analogous sum over v ∈ S_π with factor 2/(q^{2r}_v − 1) and W^{sph}_{T□,v}(1); the proof splits into the split, unramified, almost unramified and ramified cases, using Proposition A.7 (local p-adic height = Beilinson's local index), [47, Prop. 4.20], [46, Prop. 8.1] and [47, Thm. 1.1].
items.locator: §4.6, Lemma 4.31, Notation 4.32, Proposition 4.33, pp. 293–296, published version

items.name: §4.7 (Lemmas 4.34, 4.36, 4.37 and Proposition 4.35: local heights above p decay p-adically)
items.statement: Lemma 4.34: for n < p there is (t_1, t_2) with χ^♦_{π̂}(t_1)χ^♦_π(t_2) ≠ 0 such that all local heights at u | p lie in (O^×_{E_u})^{fr} ⊗_{Z_p}L; the proof builds a projective strictly semistable model X over O_K of an auxiliary Shimura variety with Drinfeld level (using [53 = LTXZZ]) whose strata X(1) = X_1 ⊔ X_2 and X(2) = X_1 ∩ X_2, and applies Theorem A.8 (the crystalline property of bi-extensions) with the Hecke ideals m = ker χ^♦_{π̂}, m′ = ker χ^♦_π. Lemma 4.36: cycles built from φ^{[e]}_{v,2} lie in the subgroup Z^r_{[|e|]}(X_L) of cycles supported on the level-[|e|] part. Lemma 4.37: there is M ≥ 0 with p^M annihilating H^1_f(K_d, T_{π,L})/N_∞H^1_f(K_d, T_{π,L}) for all d (universal norms, via [56, Theorem 6.9] and the Lubin–Tate argument of [68, §8]). Proposition 4.35: consequently the local heights at u | p lie in (O^×_{E_u})^{fr} ⊗ p^{|e_{2,v}|−M}O_L, so they tend to 0 p-adically as the U_p-iterations grow.
items.locator: §4.7, Lemmas 4.34, 4.36–4.37, Proposition 4.35, pp. 296–302, published version
items.note: This is the p-adic replacement for the vanishing of the archimedean and p-adic contributions in the complex arithmetic inner product formula. Routed to the new Part II PadicArithmeticInnerProductFormula (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: §4.8 (Remark 4.38, Lemmas 4.39–4.44 and Proposition 4.45: the limit of the height generating series)
items.statement: The height generating series is compared with a family of measures: Lemma 4.39 produces integral measures (E^{[e]}_{(g_1,g_2)})_{T□} on Γ_{F,p} interpolating p^MW^♦_{2r}b^♦_{2r}(ιχ)W_{T□}((g_1, g_2)·ι(ŝ_1t̂_1, ŝ_2t̂_2)f^{[e]}_{ιχ^{∞p}}) (4.15) and their S_π-analogues; Lemma 4.40 identifies their q-expansions with those of the Eisenstein families; Definition 4.41 and Lemma 4.42 set up the rational spaces A^K_M of automorphic forms with M-rational q-expansions; Lemma 4.43 produces the pullbacks D^{[e]}_χ and their convergence along e = N!; Lemma 4.44 shows that the classes Z^ét_{T_2}(t_2s_2g_2φ^{[N!]}_2)_L converge in H^1_f(E, V_{π̂,L}); and Proposition 4.45 shows that the sequence I_{λ,d} converges to I_λ ∈ L ⊗ A^{K^†}_O whose q-expansion is vol^♮(L)Σ_{T_1,T_2}λ_E⟨Z^ét_{T_1}(t_1s_1g_1φ_1)_L, ζ_{g_2,T_2}⟩_E q^{T_1,T_2}, with I_λ ∈ O_L ⊗ A^K_{Z_{(p)}}.
items.locator: §4.8, Remark 4.38, Lemmas 4.39–4.44, Proposition 4.45, pp. 302–313, published version
items.note: Routed to the new Part II PadicArithmeticInnerProductFormula (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Proposition 4.46 and the proof of Theorem 4.20; Remark 4.47
items.statement: Proposition 4.46: if n < p, ∂L^♦_p(π) ≠ 0 and the local zeta integrals at v ∈ R can be made nonzero, then there is λ with I_λ ≠ 0. Given this, Theorem 4.20 follows: a nonzero q^{T_2}-coefficient of (1, g_2)·I_λ is a strongly nonzero automorphic form to which Lemma 4.26 applies. Remark 4.47: the same strategy cannot give an unconditional construction of arithmetic theta lifts in Chow groups, because the semisimplicity and automorphy used for H^1(E, H^{2r−1}) are unknown for CH^r(X_L).
items.locator: Proposition 4.46, p. 313; proof of Theorem 4.20, pp. 313–314; Remark 4.47, p. 314, published version
items.note: Routed to the new Part II PadicArithmeticInnerProductFormula (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: §4.9 (Proposition 4.48 and Lemma 4.49: the p-adic doubling formula and the proof of Theorem 4.21)
items.statement: Proposition 4.48: for n < p and λ ∈ Hom_{Z_p}(Γ_{F,p}, Z_p), ⟨ϕ_1 ⊗ ϕ_2, I_λ⟩_{π,π̂} = p^M χ^♦_{π̂}(t_1s_1)χ^♦_π(t_2s_2)·∂_λL^♦_p(π)·Π_{v ∈ V^{(♦\{∞,p})}_F}Z(ϕ^†_{1,v} ⊗ ϕ_{2,v}, f^{1_v}), proved by running the doubling computation of §3.5 with the vectors (T2)–(T4) chosen so that the p-adic zeta integrals are the gamma factors of Proposition 3.32. Lemma 4.49: those zeta integrals are nonzero away from R, being C_v·L(1/2, BC(π_v))/b_{2r,v}(1) ([52 = Liu, almost unramified], [47, Prop. 3.6], Lemma 3.31). Combining Proposition 4.48 with Propositions 4.33, 4.35 and 4.45 proves Theorem 4.21, and Proposition 4.46 follows.
items.locator: §4.9, Proposition 4.48, Lemma 4.49, pp. 314–319, published version
items.note: Routed to the new Part II PadicArithmeticInnerProductFormula (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: §4.10 (Remarks 4.50–4.51: errata for Li–Liu 2021 and 2022)
items.statement: Remark 4.50: in [46] and [47] the Hecke character χ^R_{π^∨} was mistakenly identified with (χ^R_π)^c — they agree only on T^R_{Q^{ac}} ∩ R — so [46, Proposition 6.10(1)] should read χ^R_{π^∨}(s) in place of χ^R_π(s)^c, and the two elements required in S^R_{Q^{ac}} \ m^R_π should be taken in S^R_{Q^{ac}} \ m^R_{π^∨}; the proofs are unaffected. Remark 4.51: the preprint [67 = Shah, arXiv:2310.01677] shows that two formulae claimed in the proof of [46, Lemma 4.4] about Hecke correspondences of special cycles and Schwartz functions are incorrect in general; the lemma is reproved here by showing that φ^∞ ↦ Z_T(φ^∞)_{L′} defines a map of smooth H(A^∞_F)-representations into the limit of the Chow groups, which factors through CH^m(X_L)_C on L-invariants.
items.locator: §4.10, Remarks 4.50–4.51, pp. 319–320, published version
items.note: These are corrections to PAPER-LI-LIU-21 and PAPER-LI-LIU-22, recorded there as well. Routed to the new Part II PadicArithmeticInnerProductFormula (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: The cyclotomic Iwasawa objects Γ_{K,p} and the character space X_{K,p}
items.statement: For a number field K, Γ_{K,p} is the p-completion of K^×\A^{∞,×}_K/(O_K ⊗ Π_{w ∤ p}Z_w)^×, a finitely generated Z_p-module, and X_{K,p} is the rigid analytic space over Q_p with X_{K,p}(R) the continuous characters Γ_{K,p} → R^×; bounded analytic functions on X_{F,p} ⊗ L are the same as L-valued p-adic measures on Γ_{F,p}, i.e. elements of Z_p[[Γ_{F,p}]] ⊗_{Z_p}L.
items.locator: §1, p. 221–222; Remark 1.5(1), p. 223, published version
items.note: L0a plans rigid character and weight spaces, L1 the completed group rings; the ray-class group here is the standard cyclotomic one.

items.name: The unitary Shimura varieties X_L for H = U(V)
items.statement: For V of signature (n−1, 1) at one archimedean place and (n, 0) elsewhere and H = U(V), the system {X_L} indexed by neat open compact L ⊆ H(A^∞_F) consists of smooth projective schemes over E of dimension n − 1, with the usual complex uniformization; they carry Kudla's special cycles and the Hecke action of S^♦.
items.note: V6 plans canonical models for Hodge and abelian type data, which covers the existence of X_L; their integral models are imported from the unitary Part IIs of earlier extractions.

items.name: The Hochschild–Serre filtration and the absolute cycle class map
items.statement: The absolute cycle class map CH^m(X_L) → H^{2m}_ét(X_L, Q_p(m)) and the Hochschild–Serre filtration F^i with F^iH^{2r}/F^{i+1}H^{2r} a subquotient of H^i(E, H^{2r−i}_ét(X_L, Q_p(r))) (degeneration as in [31 = Jannsen]) are the input for the map ℘_π and for Nekovář's p-adic Abel–Jacobi theory.
items.locator: §4.2, pp. 278–280, published version
items.note: EDC.3 plans cycle classes in étale cohomology and R02.2 the Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence, as PAPER-LI-LIU-21 routes the same inputs.

items.name: Bloch–Kato Selmer groups H^1_f(E, V)
items.statement: The Bloch–Kato Selmer group H^1_f(E, V) ⊆ H^1(E, V) of [5 = Bloch–Kato], cut out by the unramified condition away from p and by the crystalline condition at p, in which the Selmer theta lifts live and on which the p-adic height pairing is defined.
items.locator: §1.2, p. 225; §4.2, p. 282, published version
items.note: L2 plans Selmer structures and complexes and L4 adds the finite Bloch–Kato conditions once the period rings are available.

items.name: §A.1 (étale correspondences and rings of correspondences)
items.statement: An étale correspondence on a scheme X is a diagram t : X ←^f X′ →^g X with f and g finite étale; these form a monoidal category ÉtCor(X), and EC(X) is the unital Z-algebra generated by the isomorphism classes of its objects. An R-ring of étale correspondences on X is an R-ring T with a unital R-linear map T → EC(X)_R ([51 = Liu, Definition 2.11]). Notation A.1: for S ⊆ X and t as above, S_t := f(g^{−1}(S)), extended to finite linear combinations by unions.
items.locator: §A.1, Notation A.1, pp. 320–321, published version
items.note: Routed to the new Part II SelmerComplexesAndPadicHeights (parent SelmerIwasawaCohomology).

items.name: §A.2 (continuous étale cohomology, equivariant sheaves and the functor C ↦ C_L)
items.statement: For a site S and a diagram of rings R_• one has M(S, R_•), C^+(S, R_•) and D^+(S, R_•); the case R_• = W_• : ⋯ → W/p³ → W/p² → W/p gives systems F_• with p^lF_l = 0, with lim← and the exact restrictions (−)_l. Example A.2: L(r)_X := (R lim←(μ^{⊗r}_{p•})_X) ⊗_{Z_p}L computes Jannsen's continuous étale cohomology H^q(X, L(r)) [30], and H^q(S_ét, Rπ_!L(r)_X) its variant with proper support. For a profinite G acting on S one has M_G(S, R_•), H^q_G(S, −), the forgetful map to H^q(S, −) with kernel H^q_G(S, −)_0, and C_L := (R lim← C) ⊗_W L (A.1).
items.locator: §A.2, Example A.2, (A.1), pp. 321–322, published version
items.note: D7 is the sole generic owner of continuous derived cohomology with compact coefficients, derived inverse limits and continuous Hochschild–Serre; R02.2 owns the Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence.

items.name: Definition A.3 and Lemmas A.4–A.5 (admissible objects, the Hochschild–Serre edge map and its cocycle)
items.statement: Definition A.3: C ∈ D^+_G(S, W_•) is admissible if every H^q(S, C_l) is a discrete G-module and R¹lim←_l H^q(S, C_l) has finite exponent; then H^q(S, C_L) ≅ (lim←_l H^q(S, C_l)) ⊗_W L as topological G-modules. Lemma A.4: for admissible C there is a spectral sequence H^p_cont(G, H^q(S, C_L)) ⇒ H^{p+q}_G(S, C_L), hence an edge map H^q_G(S, C_L)_0 → H¹_cont(G, H^{q−1}(S, C_L)) (generalizing [30, Cor. 3.4] rationally). Lemma A.5: for a distinguished triangle A → B → C of admissible objects and b ∈ H^q_G(S, B_L) whose image in H^q(S, C_L) vanishes, the image of ν(b) in H¹_cont(G, H^{q−1}(S, C_L)/H^{q−1}(S, B_L)) is represented by the cocycle g ↦ ga − a for any a ∈ H^q(S, A_L) with μ(a) = β(b).
items.locator: Definition A.3, Lemmas A.4–A.5, pp. 322–324, published version
items.note: Lemma A.5 is used only in §B.6, to compare the crystalline and étale edge maps. The proof of Lemma A.5 contains three misprints (sourceIssues E4), and Lemma A.4 is stated over Z_{p•} although it is applied to W_•-objects (sourceIssues E5). Routed to the new Part II SelmerComplexesAndPadicHeights (parent SelmerIwasawaCohomology).

items.name: §A.3 (homologically trivial cycles, the localisation diagram (A.2) and the maps κ_c, κ_{c′})
items.statement: For X projective smooth over K of pure dimension n − 1, Z^d(X)^0_L := Ker(Z^d(X)_L → H^{2d}(X_K̄, L(d))). For c ∈ Z^d(X)^0_L and c′ ∈ Z^{d′}(X)^0_L with d + d′ = n and disjoint supports, choosing disjoint closed Z, Z′ of pure codimensions d, d′ containing them gives the diagram (A.2) of localisation sequences for U = X∖Z and U′ = X∖Z′; c gives κ_c : L → H^{2d}(Z_K̄, i^!L(d)) landing in the kernel to H^{2d}(X_K̄, L(d)), and c′ gives κ_{c′} : H^{2d−2}(Z′_K̄, L(d−1)) → L vanishing on the image of H^{2d−2}(X_K̄, L(d−1)).
items.locator: §A.3, (A.2), pp. 324–325, published version
items.note: The printed twists in the last clause read L(d) (sourceIssues E6). The refined cycle classes and Gysin maps used here are planned in EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves EDC.3. Routed to the new Part II SelmerComplexesAndPadicHeights (parent SelmerIwasawaCohomology).

items.name: §A.3 (the bi-extension of two cycles and the classes [E_c], [E^{c′}], [E^c_{c′}])
items.statement: Pulling (A.2) back along κ_c and pushing it out along κ_{c′}(1) gives a diagram in M_K(L) with exact rows 0 → L(1) → E_{c′} → H^{2d−1}(X_K̄, L(d)) → 0 and 0 → L(1) → E^c_{c′} → E_c → 0 and columns E_{c′} → E^c_{c′} → L and H^{2d−1}(X_K̄, L(d)) → E_c → L, independent of the choice of Z and Z′; it yields [E_c] ∈ H¹(K, H^{2d−1}(X_K̄, L(d))), [E^∨_{c′}(1)] = [E^{c′}] ∈ H¹(K, H^{2d′−1}(X_K̄, L(d′))) and [E^c_{c′}] ∈ H¹(K, E_{c′}).
items.locator: §A.3, pp. 325–326, published version
items.note: Routed to the new Part II SelmerComplexesAndPadicHeights (parent SelmerIwasawaCohomology).

items.name: §A.4 (Nekovář's and Beilinson's local indices, Remark A.6 and Proposition A.7)
items.statement: For K non-archimedean with residue characteristic ≠ p and vanishing cycle classes, [E^c_{c′}] comes from H¹(K, L(1)) = K̂^× ⊗_Ẑ L, and its preimage is Nekovář's local index ⟨c, c′⟩^N_{X,K} [56]. Beilinson's local index ⟨c, c′⟩^B_{X,K} is the image of γ ∪ γ′ under the Mayer–Vietoris coboundary H^{2n−2}(U ∩ U′, L(n)) → H^{2n−1}(X, L(n)) and the trace map, for lifts γ, γ′ of the refined cycle classes [1 = Beilinson, §2], [46, App. B]. Remark A.6: under the canonical identification H¹(Spec K, Q_p(1)) ≃ Q_p used in [1] and [46], a uniformizer of K goes to −1, not 1 ([23, 2.1.3], [57, II.(2.16.1)]). Proposition A.7: ⟨c, c′⟩^N_{X,K} = ⟨c, c′⟩^B_{X,K}, which is [66 = Scholl, Theorem 5.3].
items.locator: §A.4, Remark A.6, Proposition A.7, p. 326, published version
items.note: Proposition A.7 is what lets §4.6 quote the complex-case local index computations of Li–Liu for the p-adic height. Routed to the new Part II SelmerComplexesAndPadicHeights (parent SelmerIwasawaCohomology).

items.name: Theorem A.8 and Remark A.9 (the crystalline property of bi-extensions)
items.statement: Let 𝒳 be a proper strictly semistable model of X over O_K with special fibre X and strata X^{(h)}, and n < p. Let T be an L-ring of étale correspondences on 𝒳 and m, m′ maximal ideals of T with ⨁_{h>1,q≥0}(H^q_cris(X^{(h)}/W) ⊗ L)_m = ⨁_{h>1,q≥0}(H^q_cris(X^{(h)}/W) ⊗ L)_{m′} = 0 (A.3). Then there are t ∈ T∖m and t′ ∈ T∖m′, depending only on 𝒳, such that for all c ∈ Z^d(X)^0_L and c′ ∈ Z^{d′}(X)^0_L with d + d′ = n satisfying (1) (supp 𝒞)_t ∩ (supp 𝒞′)_{t′} = ∅ for all correspondences and (2) codim_{X^{(h)}}(supp 𝒞′) ≥ d′ for every h ≥ 1, the three classes [E_{t^*c}], [E^∨_{t′^*c′}(1)] and [E^{t^*c}_{t′^*c′}] are crystalline (lie in H¹_f). Remark A.9: for T = L and a proper smooth model this says that E^c_{c′} is crystalline whenever the closures of the supports are disjoint, confirming the conjecture after [68, Theorem 8.7] for n < p; the statement fails for strictly semistable models without the Hecke localisation.
items.locator: Theorem A.8, Remark A.9, p. 327; strategy, pp. 327–328, published version
items.note: The strategy follows Sato [65]: compare the syntomic Abel–Jacobi map with one defined through log rigid cohomology (Proposition B.9) and kill the cycle class after localisation at m′. Routed to the new Part II SelmerComplexesAndPadicHeights (parent SelmerIwasawaCohomology).

items.name: §A.6 (de Rham and crystalline representations, Weil–Deligne representations, Remark A.10 and Definition A.11)
items.statement: For K/Q_p finite and V a de Rham L-representation of G_K one has D_dR(V) with its filtration and, for each τ : K → Q̄_p, Fontaine's Weil–Deligne representation WD(V)_τ on D_dR(V) ⊗_{L ⊗ K,1⊗τ}Q̄_p, whose isomorphism class is independent of τ; V is crystalline if D_cris(V) is free of the right rank. Remark A.10: for crystalline V the geometric Frobenius characteristic polynomial on WD(V)_τ is that of φ on D_cris(V). Definition A.11: V is pure of weight μ if the geometric Frobenius eigenvalues on gr^iWD(V)_τ are Weil |κ|^{μ+i}-numbers for every i.
items.locator: §A.6, Remark A.10, Definition A.11, pp. 328–329, published version
items.note: R06.1 constructs B_dR, B_cris, B_st and R06.2 the period functors and admissibility; the Weil–Deligne functor is the one of [70, §1].

items.name: Definition A.12 and Lemmas A.13–A.14 (the Panchishkin condition)
items.statement: Definition A.12 (after [56, 6.7]): V satisfies the Panchishkin condition if there is a (necessarily unique) subrepresentation V⁺ ⊆ V with F⁰D_dR(V⁺) = 0 and D_dR(V/V⁺)/F⁰D_dR(V/V⁺) = 0. Lemma A.13: for crystalline V this is equivalent to: the negative-slope part D⁺_cris(V) is weakly admissible and (D⁺_cris(V) ⊗_{K_0}K) ⊕ F⁰D_dR(V) ≅ D_dR(V) (A.4) splits the Hodge filtration (using Colmez–Fontaine [11]). Lemma A.14: purity of a given nonzero weight and the Panchishkin condition are both stable under extensions of crystalline representations.
items.locator: Definition A.12, Lemmas A.13–A.14, p. 329, published version
items.note: (A.4) is the Hodge splitting that Nekovář's height pairing needs at the p-adic places; Lemma 4.14 verifies it for V_{π,L}. Routed to the new Part II SelmerComplexesAndPadicHeights (parent SelmerIwasawaCohomology).

items.name: §A.7 (the p-adic height pairing of cycles, its local decomposition and Remark A.15)
items.statement: For K a number field, X proper smooth of pure dimension n − 1, and L[G_K]-submodules V ⊆ H^{2d−1}(X_K̄, L(d)), V′ ⊆ H^{2d′−1}(X_K̄, L(d′)) satisfying (V1) H^i(K_u, V) = H^i(K_u, V′) = 0 for u ∤ p∞, (V2) semistability and purity of weight −1 at u | p, and (V3) the Panchishkin condition at u | p, Nekovář's theory gives ⟨ , ⟩_{(V,V′),K} : H¹_f(K, V) × H¹_f(K, V′) → Γ_{K,p} ⊗_{Z_p}L; with the Abel–Jacobi maps Z^d_V(X)^0_L → H¹_f(K, V) (using [58, Theorem 3.1] and (V2)) this gives a pairing of cycles (A.5). For cycles with disjoint supports it decomposes as Σ_{u ∤ ∞}⟨c, c′⟩_{(V,V′),K_u} with ⟨c, c′⟩_{(V,V′),K_u} = ⟨c, c′⟩^N_{X_u,K_u} away from p [56, §4]. Remark A.15: for u | p, [E^c_{c′}] ∈ H¹_f(K_u, E_{c′}) if and only if ⟨c, c′⟩_{(V,V′),K_u} ∈ O^×_{K_u} ⊗_{Z_p}L.
items.locator: §A.7, (A.5), Remark A.15, pp. 330–331, published version
items.note: Remark A.15 is how Theorem A.8 enters the main argument (Lemma 4.34). Routed to the new Part II SelmerComplexesAndPadicHeights (parent SelmerIwasawaCohomology).

items.name: §B.1 (tubular neighbourhoods, the functor f^!_{(U,X)}, log structures and admissible embedding systems)
items.statement: For 𝒵 of finite type over O_{K′} one has the formal completion, the Berkovich generic fibre 𝒵_η, the tubular neighbourhood ]X[_{𝒵_η} of a subscheme, the quasi-étale site [2, §3] and the specialization map s_{(X,𝒵)} : ]X[_{𝒵_η,qét} → X_ét (using [3, Prop. 2.1]). Definition B.1: f^!_{(U,X)} is the kernel of id → g_*g^* for g the open immersion ]X∖U[ → ]X[; Remark B.2: it is exact, and in general no functor on X_ét is compatible with it under Rs_*. Lemma B.3: there is a canonical transformation F_!F^*Rs_{(X,𝒵)*} → Rs_{(X,𝒵)*}f^!_{(U,X)}. Log conventions: L^Y_X, W^triv, W[t]°, W°, κ° and O^can_{K′}; embedding systems {(X^⋆, M^⋆) ↪ (Z^⋆, N^⋆)} and admissible ones in the strictly semistable case, following [22, §§2.1, 5.1].
items.locator: §B.1, Definition B.1, Remark B.2, Lemma B.3, pp. 331–333, published version
items.note: Routed to PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology RD.4 as a source; the log-geometric objects are planned in CrystallineCohomology CR.5.

items.name: §B.2 (rigid de Rham–Witt complexes ω_X, ω̃_X, their proper-support versions and the comparison with Wω^•_X)
items.statement: For a fine log-scheme (X, L) over κ° one defines ω_X := Ru_*Rs^⋆_*(Ω^•_{(Y^⋆,M^⋆)/W°} ⊗ O_{]X^⋆[}) and ω̃_X with (Z^⋆, N^⋆) over W^triv, independent of the embedding system, giving the monodromy triangle ω_X[−1] → ω̃_X → ω_X →^N ω_X (B.1); the versions ω_{(U,X)}, ω̃_{(U,X)} with f^!_{(U,X)} give (B.2) and the triangle of triangles (B.3). The log crystalline complexes C_{(X,L)/W°} = Wω^•_X and C̃_{(X,L)/W°} = Wω̃^•_X of Hyodo–Kato give (B.4), and [4, (1.9.2)] gives the equivalences ω_X ≅ Wω^•_{X,K_0}, ω̃_X ≅ Wω̃^•_{X,K_0} (B.5) matching (B.1) with (B.4), hence the map F_!F^*Wω̃^•_{X,K_0} → ω̃_{(U,X)} (B.6). The cohomological variant Ξ^•_{Z^⋆} gives ω⁺_X ≃ WΞ^•_{X,K_0} (Sato [65, Def. 8.3, Prop. 8.4]) with the maps (B.9)–(B.10).
items.locator: §B.2, (B.1)–(B.10), pp. 333–337, published version
items.note: Routed to CrystallineCohomology CR.4–CR.6 as a source: the relative and log de Rham–Witt complexes are planned there, the rigid-analytic (convergent) model and the proper-support versions are not.

items.name: §B.3 (log rigid cohomology with proper support, Definition B.4, and the weight spectral sequences with Lemmas B.5–B.6)
items.statement: For X proper strictly semistable over κ°, H^q(X_ét, ω_X) = H^q_conv(X/W°) ≅ H^q_rig(X/W°) [22, Thm. 5.3(ii)]. Definition B.4 introduces, ad hoc, H^q_rig((U, X)/W°) := H^q(X_ét, ω_{(U,X)}) with pushforwards in U and the long exact sequence (B.11). The filtration P_• on Ω^•_{(Z^⋆,N^⋆)/W^triv} gives weight spectral sequences E(X), E(U), E(X∖U) (B.12) and E(U, X) (B.13) = E_c(U) with E_1-terms ⨁_j H^{q−2j−k}_{c,rig}(U^{(2j+k+1)}/K_0) converging to H^q_rig((U, X)/W°). Lemma B.5: if dim(X^{(h)}∖U^{(h)}) ≤ d − h for all h then H^q_rig((U, X)/W°) → H^q_rig(X/W°) is an isomorphism for q ≥ 2d, and the corresponding E_1-terms agree for q ≥ 2d − |k| and in the stated summand for (0, 2d−1). Lemma B.6: a spectral sequence E⁺_c(U)^{−k,q+k}_1 = H^{q−k}_{c,rig}(U^{(k+1)}/K_0) (k ≥ 0) abutting to H^q(X_ét, ω⁺_{(U,X)}), compatible with the projections.
items.locator: §B.3, Definition B.4, (B.11)–(B.13), Lemmas B.5–B.6, pp. 337–339, published version
items.note: Routed to PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology RD.4 as a source: RD.4 plans rigid cohomology with compact support, not its logarithmic version with proper support nor its weight spectral sequence.

items.name: §B.4 (log syntomic complexes, the Abel–Jacobi map α_q, Definition B.7 and Lemma B.8)
items.statement: For 0 ≤ d < p − 1, Kato's log syntomic complexes S(d)_𝒳 satisfy S(d)_𝒳 ≅ τ_{≤d}i^*Rj_*(μ^{⊗d}_{p•})_X ([34], [72]) and give the map RΓ(X_ét, F_!F^*S(d)_{𝒳,Q_p}) → RΓ_c(U, Q_p(d)) (B.14) and, through the Hochschild–Serre edge map, α_q : H^q(X_ét, F_!F^*S(d)_{𝒳,Q_p})^♡ → H¹(K, H^{q−1}_c(Ū, Q_p) ⊗ B_cris) (B.15). The comparison (B.16) with the crystalline complexes C_{𝒳/W^triv}, C_{𝒳/W[t]°} gives F_!F^*S(d)_{𝒳,Q_p} → ω̃_{(U,X)} (B.17). Definition B.7: U is d-dense if dim(X^{(h)}∖U^{(h)}) ≤ d − h for every h ≥ 1. Lemma B.8: for d-dense U the composite to H^{2d}_rig((U, X)/W°) kills the ♡-part (using [65, Prop. A.3.1, Lemma 9.5]), whence the map ρ_{2d} to H^{2d−1}_rig((U, X)/W°)/N (B.18).
items.locator: §B.4, (B.14)–(B.18), Definition B.7, Lemma B.8, pp. 340–343, published version

items.name: Proposition B.9 (the kernel comparison)
items.statement: Suppose n < p, 1 ≤ d < p − 1 and U d-dense. Then there is a finite extension K_U/K in K̄, with K_𝒳 = K, such that Ker(ρ_{2d}) ⊆ Ker(res_{K_U} ∘ α_{2d}): a class in the syntomic cohomology with proper support that dies in log rigid cohomology has vanishing p-adic Abel–Jacobi image after restriction to K_U.
items.locator: Proposition B.9, p. 343; proof, §B.6, pp. 350–351, published version

items.name: Lemma B.10, Proposition B.11 and the proof of Theorem A.8 (§B.4)
items.statement: For t ∈ T put 𝒰_t := 𝒳∖((𝒳∖𝒰)_{t^∨}), and let I ⊆ T be the annihilator of ⨁_{h>1,q}H^q_rig(X^{(h)}/K_0)_L. Lemma B.10: for d-dense U and t ∈ I^{4n−5}, t^* annihilates the kernel of H^{2d−1}_rig((U_t, X)/W°)_L/N → H^{2d−1}(X_ét, ω⁺_{(U_t,X)})_L, because the weight-graded pieces of that kernel are subquotients of the cohomology of the deeper strata. Proposition B.11: for n < p, d-dense 𝒰 and t ∈ I^{4n−5}, every c ∈ Z^d(X)^0_L whose closure of support lies in 𝒰_t satisfies res_{K_U}(t^*β_c) ∈ H¹_f(K_U, H^{2d−1}_c(Ū, L(d))), where β_c is the Abel–Jacobi image of the cycle class; the proof uses Sato's p-adic étale Tate twists T(d)_𝒳 and refined cycle classes ([64, Defs. 4.2.4, 5.1.2], [65, Prop. 9.10]), the triangle (B.20), Lemma B.10 and Proposition B.9. Theorem A.8 follows by applying Proposition B.11 three times, using the purity of H^{2d′−1}(X_K̄, L(d′))_{m′} (C_st and Mokrane's weight spectral sequence) and [56, Prop. 1.25] for the exactness property (∗), the ideal J′, the subgroup H¹_♯ and the pushout (B.21).
items.locator: §B.4, Lemma B.10, Proposition B.11, (B.20)–(B.21), pp. 343–347, published version
items.note: The proof of Theorem A.8 prints H^{2d−1}_c(Ū_t, L(d)) where Proposition B.11 gives H^{2d−1}_c(Ū, L(d)) (sourceIssues E7). Routed to the new Part II SelmerComplexesAndPadicHeights (parent SelmerIwasawaCohomology).

items.name: §B.5 ((φ,N)-modules, successive homotopy fibres, the rings 𝒦 and B̂⁺_st, and Lemmas B.13–B.14)
items.statement: A (φ,N)-module in a W-linear category is an object with a semi-linear φ and a linear N satisfying Nφ = pφN. Definition B.12: the successive homotopy fibre of a finite complex C^0 → ⋯ → C^m in a triangulated category, which inherits a (φ,N)-structure. With R_l the PD envelope of O_K/p^l in W[t]/p^l and P_l the ring of [34, (3.2)], [71, §1.6], one puts 𝒦 := (lim←R_l) ⊗_W K_0 and B̂⁺_st := (lim←P_l) ⊗_W K_0. Lemma B.13: B⁺_st ≅ (B̂⁺_st)^{N-nilp}, B̂⁺_st is flat over 𝒦, and N is surjective on B̂⁺_st. Hence for a nilpotent (φ,N)-module D over K_0 one has two edge maps from D/ND and from (D ⊗ 𝒦)/N(D ⊗ 𝒦) to H¹(K, (D ⊗ B⁺_st)^{N=0}) (using (B̂⁺_st)^{G_K} = 𝒦, [7, Cor. 4.1.3]). Lemma B.14: on the φ = p^r part the second factors through the first via the specialization 𝒦 → K_0 at t = 0 (as in [44, Lemma 2.6]); Remark B.15 notes this fails without the Frobenius restriction and records the open question about Ker(𝒦 → K_0) ⊆ N(B̂_st)^{G_K}.
items.locator: §B.5, Definition B.12, Lemmas B.13–B.14, Remark B.15, pp. 347–350, published version

items.name: §B.6 (the strict semistable alteration and Lemmas B.16–B.17)
items.statement: By de Jong [12, Thm. 6.5] there are a finite K′/K, a projective strictly semistable 𝒳′ over O_{K′} and a generically finite alteration A : 𝒳′ → 𝒳 making (𝒳′, A^{−1}𝒰) a strict semistable pair; 𝒰′ ⊆ 𝒳′ is the open subscheme with U′ = A^{−1}U and 𝒳′∖𝒰′ flat. Lemma B.16: for n < p the syntomic-to-rigid composite kills the ♡-part in every degree q for the alteration, giving ρ′_q (B.22) — this does not follow from Lemma B.8, since U′ need not be d-dense. Lemma B.17: Ker(ρ′_q) ⊆ Ker(α′_q) for every q. Proposition B.9 follows with K_U = K′, because H^q_c(Ū, Q_p) → H^q_c(Ū′, Q_p) admits a section by Poincaré duality.
items.locator: §B.6, Lemmas B.16–B.17, pp. 350–351, published version

items.name: §B.6 (the strata 𝒱(h), Galois embedding systems, the barred syntomic and crystalline complexes, and Lemmas B.18–B.25)
items.statement: With 𝒱 = 𝒳∖𝒰, 𝒱(h) the h-fold intersections (𝒱(0) = 𝒳, 𝒱(−1) = (𝒰,𝒳)), Lemma B.18 identifies the pullback of the log structure with L^{V(h)}_{𝒱(h)}, and Remark B.19 resolves F_!(μ^{⊗r}_{p•})_Ū by the strata, so that all objects for h = −1 are successive homotopy fibres. Using a Galois embedding system for O^can_{K̄}/W[t]° one builds the G_K-equivariant complexes B̄(r)_{𝒱(h)} (B.24)–(B.25), C̄_{𝒱(h)/W^triv}, C̄_{𝒱(h)/W[t]°} with the triangle (B.26), the syntomic S̄(r)_{𝒱(h)} and the period map π_r (B.29), and their unbarred versions with (B.30)–(B.32). Lemma B.20: ω_{𝒱(h)} ≅ C_{𝒱(h)/W°,K_0}, so H^q_rig(V(h)/W°) ≅ H^q(X_ét, C_{𝒱(h)/W°,K_0}) compatibly with N. Lemma B.21: admissibility of C_{𝒱(h)/W[t]°}, C̄_{𝒱(h)/W[t]°} and C̄_{𝒱(h)/W^triv}, the base changes H^q(C_{𝒱(h)/W[t]°,K_0}) ≅ H^q(C_{𝒱(h)/W°,K_0}) ⊗_{K_0}𝒦 and H^q(C_{𝒱(h)/W[t]°,K_0}) ⊗_𝒦 B̂⁺_st ≅ H^q(C̄_{𝒱(h)/W[t]°,K_0}), and H^q(C̄_{𝒱(h)/W^triv,K_0}) ≅ (H^q(C_{𝒱(h)/W°,K_0}) ⊗ B⁺_st)^{N=0}. Lemma B.22: the C_st-comparison for all strata including h = −1 ([71, Thm. 4.10.2], [75 = Yamashita] for h = −1), Lemma B.23 its compatibility with ξ_r and π_r, Lemma B.24 the factorisation of (B.14) and (B.17) through S(d)_{𝒱(−1)}, and Lemma B.25 the Abel–Jacobi version of Lemma B.23; the proof of Lemma B.17 then combines Lemma A.5, Lemma B.14 and Lemma B.21 in the diagram (B.40).

items.name: Tsuji's C_st comparison and the Hyodo–Kato complexes
items.statement: The semistable comparison theorem H^q_ét(X_K̄, Q_p) ⊗ B_st ≅ H^q_{log-cris}(X/W°) ⊗ B_st with its Frobenius, monodromy and Galois structures [71, Thm. 4.10.2, Cors. 4.8.8, 4.9.2], the log crystalline (Hyodo–Kato) complexes Wω^•_X of [27], [28], and Mokrane's weight spectral sequence [55], are the inputs of Lemma B.22 and of the purity step in the proof of Theorem A.8.
items.locator: §§B.2, B.6 and the proof of Theorem A.8, pp. 334, 346, 360–361, published version

items.name: de Jong's alteration theorem
items.statement: Every variety over a discretely valued field admits, after a finite extension, a generically finite alteration by a projective strictly semistable scheme, and a pair (X, U) admits a strict semistable alteration [12, Theorem 6.5, §6.3].
items.locator: §B.6, p. 350, published version
